# Nationwide Traffic Drop and Latency Rise Due to Core DNS Degradation

- **Classification:** incident
- **Root cause:** core_degradation at `CORE-DNS-01`
- **Confidence:** medium (Core KPIs and alarms match DNS degradation, but direct internal fault mechanism lacks specific confirmation.)
- **Impact:** 2026-09-21 12:30 to 2026-09-21 14:11
- **Cause time:** 2026-09-21 12:30
- **Affected:** CORE-DNS-01, S-SAH-001, S-SAH-002, S-SAH-003, S-SAH-004

## Summary

Core DNS degradation on CORE-DNS-01 caused nationwide traffic drop and latency rise.

Nationwide traffic fell and latency rose due to core DNS degradation between 12:30 and 14:11.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-21 12:30: Nationwide DNS query success drop and latency anomaly begins. [ALR-0024, ANM-000229, ANM-000230]
- 2026-09-21 12:35: Major DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE alarm raised on CORE-DNS-01. [ALM-000365]
- 2026-09-21 14:11: DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE alarm cleared and service recovered. [ALM-000365]

## Evidence

- CORE-DNS-01 query_success_pct dropped and resolution_ms spiked starting at 12:30. [T1, T2, ANM-000229, ANM-000230]
- Major alarm DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE was triggered on CORE-DNS-01 at 12:35 and cleared at 14:11. [T3, ALM-000365]
- No maintenance window was scheduled on CORE-DNS-01 and its parents during the window. [T6]
- No external events were reported across all regions between 12:00 and 18:00. [T9]

## Hypotheses

1. **core_degradation** at CORE-DNS-01: confirmed. Core KPIs and major DNS timeout alarms directly match core DNS degradation signatures. [RB-DNS-DEGRADATION#02, ANM-000229, ALM-000365]
2. **bad_change** at CORE-DNS-01: rejected. Change CHG-2026-0056 was applied at 11:12, but degradation started 78 minutes later, ruling out immediate bad change impact. [CHG-2026-0056, ALR-0024]

## Ruled out

- ALR-0025: Occurred later from 16:45 to 21:00 and was localized to 3 sites in SAH, unrelated to the nationwide midday event.
- CHG-2026-0057: Applied to CORE-AMF-01, which did not exhibit the direct core DNS KPI degradation signature.
- CHG-2026-0058: Applied to CORE-UPF-01, which did not exhibit the direct core DNS KPI degradation signature.

## Recommended actions

- Investigate internal resource exhaustion or transient node faults on CORE-DNS-01 during the incident window.
- Monitor core DNS telemetry for recurring degradation patterns.

confounders.why: Harmless software_upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 completed 72 min before the degradation; the DNS KPIs stayed normal until the onset and the same patch on other core nodes did nothing.

truth.notes: trap=change_on_root_node; CORE-DNS-01 degraded for about 99 min; nationwide latency up, volume down, RRC unaffected. Trap: a software upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 itself ran 72 min before the onset, so a hasty investigator blames the change. Settled by: (1) the DNS and RRC KPIs were normal for 72 min after the upgrade, while a configuration change takes effect at once; (2) the same patch under the same ticket went onto CORE-AMF-01 and CORE-UPF-01 at the same time and both stayed healthy; (3) the degradation ended by itself, with no rollback or other change at the recovery.
